profile.campus: Red Oak Campus, Compass Datacenters Dallas-Fort Worth market
profile.address: Ellis County, TX (Red Oak development campus, westernmost row)
profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record is one of eleven adjacent building footprints in Compass Datacenters Red Oak development, a wholesale data center campus in Ellis County, Texas, just south of the Dallas-Fort Worth core. This particular footprint sits in the westernmost row of the campus, second from the north among five buildings arranged along that row. Compass Datacenters own market materials describe this campus, part of its Dallas-Fort Worth market, as a 360 megawatt development that was still nearing completion as of the most recent site content reviewed, with a confirmed 200 million dollar expansion phase announced in April 2024 that added two buildings totaling more than 500,000 square feet. A separate July 2026 company news item states that Red Oak now hosts seven data centers total, though that figure appears to describe the city of Red Oak as a whole rather than Compass own building count specifically, so it should not be read as confirming exactly how many of the eleven OpenStreetMap footprints in this cluster are Compass-operated versus operated by other companies also active in the area. Compass Datacenters was founded in 2011 by Chris Crosby, a former Digital Realty senior executive who remains the company CEO, and completed its first data center, a 1.2 megawatt facility, in 2012. The company is headquartered in Dallas, Texas, and describes its current ownership, per its own about-us page, as Ontario Teachers Pension Plan, RedBird Capital Partners, and company management. Beyond Dallas-Fort Worth, Compass 2026 markets list includes active developments in Chicago Hoffman Estates, Northern Virginia Loudoun County, Toronto, and Milan, plus a newly broken-ground site in Meridian, Mississippi, alongside earlier markets including Minneapolis and Nashville that the company has since exited or transferred to independent ownership. Separately, Compass donated 12.6 million dollars to fund a 40,000 square foot workforce-training replica data center at 300 Houston School Road in Red Oak, operated by Texas State Technical College, a distinct facility from the wholesale buildings mapped here that should not be confused with them. No per-building capacity, square footage, tenant, or year-built figure could be confirmed for this specific structure within the campus, and no local government permit or tax-abatement record could be retrieved this session, so those figures are deliberately omitted rather than estimated from the campus-wide totals above.

reading.body:
Compass Red Oak Campus is a multi-phase hyperscale build-out in Ellis County, Texas, south of Dallas, owned by Brookfield Infrastructure Partners and Ontario Teachers Pension Plan following their 2023 acquisition of Compass Datacenters. The operator has not published a current operating capacity for this specific campus. The original 2020 groundbreaking announcement targeted 350 MW of IT load at full build-out across a then-165-acre site; subsequent expansions have grown the approved campus footprint to roughly 800 to 830 acres as of May 2026, with named phases including completed million-square-foot buildings and additional phases under construction or planned through 2026, but no single confirmed current megawatt figure for the operating campus was located in available sources.

This registry maps 11 separate facility rows at this campus location; without distinguishing building names or numbers in the source data, and given conflicting building-naming conventions and address assignments across aggregators and trade press, no individual row can be reliably assigned to a specific named building or street address. The campus sits at coordinates shared with four other mapped rows in a geographic cluster. Texas as a state hosts 133 mapped data center facilities, of which only 18 have published capacity figures totaling 468.41 MW; this campus contributes nothing to that published total and ranks outside the top 18 by confirmed published capacity.

Because the operator has not published current operating capacity, the campus cannot yet be read as a confirmed constraint on AI scaling or supply. The 350 MW full-build-out target from 2020 represents a future state, not confirmed current delivery. If that full target is eventually commissioned, the campus would rank as one of Texas's larger single sites, but that remains a plan rather than an operational fact. The recent 830-acre expansion approval and ongoing construction phases suggest continued build-out activity, but without published megawatt commitments by phase or completion date, the campus's material impact on grid and AI deployment timelines remains unquantified in public data.
